description: Create this application's Postgres database now, while the project is still being written, so it is built and tested against the real thing instead of SQLite or mock data. A later deploy reuses it, so what was tested is what goes live. Safe to call twice. Skip it when the project stores nothing, or already points at a database the user chose (a DATABASE_URL in .env that is not localhost, or a provider they named): the answer is a 409 own_database. It counts against the plan's allowance; a 402 database_limit is not a rate limit, so do not retry, say what it says and let the user choose. If the call is refused or blocked, do not look for another route: tell the user, who can approve it or press Create database on the application's page in the console, then carry on with `database_env_to_file`. The connection string is not returned: call `database_env_to_file` to put it in .env. Tell the user what was created and on which account.
name: database_create
title: Create the application's database now
